manifest.sampling: SHA256(seed:dataset:id) ascending; first 24 per dataset classify, first 6 per dataset execute; no difficulty strata
manifest.candidates: selected route plus main-model low and high, deduplicated; no universal fixed-medium baseline
manifest.tools: disabled; fresh ephemeral thread; no benchmark gold or tests in model input; Python output literal or full module in JSON answer
manifest.verifier: CRUXEval Python literal equality (stricter format than official expression grader); HumanEval+ pinned HF check(candidate)
manifest.evaluation: single-turn categorical route selection using actual Jev scores; no task execution tools or expert review; no gold route labels

accounting.note: Observed total is a lower bound; unknown failure usage is not zero. Input includes cache, output includes reasoning.

findings.explanation: Prompt says subsequence; all three candidates implement a non-contiguous [ [] ] subsequence, whereas gold requires nesting in the original sequence.
Prompt explicitly permits a-z/A-Z as first character. Gold accepts accented é through isalpha(). Raw scores retained.

accountingNotes: One Jev unavailable attempt, one harness false rejection of userMessage, one unclassified incomplete model turn, two confirmed serverOverloaded turns. All retained; resumed successes are separate observations.
Comparison uses first valid graded completion per task/route and excludes unavailable attempts from task-correctness scores. Therefore this is conditional correctness, not first-attempt availability.

Fresh ephemeral thread per call, benchmark tool use disabled, local skills disabled. Latency includes thread creation and archive, excluding verifier and App Server startup; selected route adds successful Jev classification latency.

Each task/route graded once. Hash sample is not difficulty-stratified; this is a diagnostic pilot, not an overall benchmark score or proof of optimal routing. Astra, long tasks, phase changes, and automatic expert review were not exercised.

def greatest_common_divisor(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """Return the greatest common divisor of two integers a and b.

    >>> greatest_common_divisor(3, 5)
    1
    >>> greatest_common_divisor(25, 15)
    5
    """
    a, b = abs(a), abs(b)
    while b:
        a, b = b, a % b
    return a

def greatest_common_divisor(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """Return the nonnegative greatest common divisor of a and b.

    >>> greatest_common_divisor(3, 5)
    1
    >>> greatest_common_divisor(25, 15)
    5
    """
    a, b = abs(a), abs(b)
    while b:
        a, b = b, a % b
    return a
